DrainageAreaClass.notes: Watershed drainage area class. Breakpoints 10 and 100 km2 are fixed constants.
DrainageAreaClass.rationale: Drainage area is the primary scaling variable for channel geometry, discharge and assemblage composition. 10 km2 separates headwaters from wadeable small streams; 100 km2 separates small streams from larger wadeable rivers. Both are conventional round-number breaks in NRSA and NHDPlus practice, not sample quantiles.

ChannelSlopeClass.notes: Reach channel slope class. Breakpoints 0.5 and 2 percent are fixed constants.
ChannelSlopeClass.rationale: Channel slope controls stream power, substrate sorting and channel type. 0.5 and 2 percent are the conventional low gradient, moderate and steep breaks used in Rosgen-family and Montgomery-Buffington channel typing. National median slope is near 0.13 percent, so this ladder is eligible in roughly half of L3 ecoregions; it is screened where it qualifies and excluded with a recorded reason where it does not.

ElevationClass.notes: Mean watershed elevation class. Breakpoints 300 and 1000 m are fixed constants.
ElevationClass.rationale: Elevation proxies thermal regime, precipitation phase and growing season length. 300 and 1000 m are conventional lowland, upland and montane breaks. Within a single ecoregion this often collapses to two populated classes, which the eligibility screen handles.

NhdDrainageAreaClass.notes: NHDPlus V2 total drainage area. Adopted by the national scale analysis (rule STRAT-10).

NhdSlopeClass.notes: NHDPlus V2 flowline slope. Adopted by the national scale analysis (rule STRAT-10).

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 10 curves are fitted to least-disturbed stations of this ecoregion. 2 curves are fitted to this ecoregion's own streams under the documented regional screen, which relaxes agriculture only. 10 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 2 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 2 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 9 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. 1 function rests on a method adopted from EASI's national screening method (provisional), because no reference pool, national donor, model, published benchmark or flagged transfer supported the function in this ecoregion. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: The pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 0.30 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. This ecoregion under the regional screen: The pool is not stable, since removing one station changes whether a valid curve can be built. The Level II pool (6.2): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The Level I pool (6): The curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). The NARS-9 pool (WMT): The pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 0.33 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. No other basis supports it either. National reference: 29 matched national donors, but the curve on this pool would be the engine's fallback ramp: the pool's lower quartile sits at or below zero on a scale that cannot go negative (curve status degenerate_q25), and a fallback curve is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). 41 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the donor pool is not stable, since one station moves a quartile by 0.25 of the interquartile range, more than 0.20. Modeled reference: The model registry holds no approved specification for this metric. Published benchmark: Every published biological criterion in the STAF assessment library is scored on a state-specific field index (Michigan Procedure 51, the Carolina IBI scores, the Wisconsin and Minnesota IBIs), none of which can be computed from NRSA data, so none measures the same quantity as this metric. EPA's own NRSA benchmarks are set on its multimetric indices, which this assessment carries as metrics of their own; an index benchmark is never applied to one of the metrics the index is built from. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.
